record.title: Eswatini frontier protest blockades on King Mswati’s birthday in April 2022
record.scope: Reported disruption at several South Africa–Eswatini posts; confirmed same-day restoration relates specifically to Ngwenya–Oshoek.
record.crossings: Ngwenya/Oshoek and Golela in News24 reporting; Mananga and Jeppes Reef additionally in SABC reporting.
record.direction: Cross-border flow affected; direction-specific enforcement not systematically reported.
record.movement: Cross-border traffic at the affected posts; exact passenger/freight shares are not documented.
record.exceptions: No documented systematic exceptions; disruption does not establish complete impermeability at every post.
record.imposing_authority: EFF members and Eswatini pro-democracy organisations and supporters; non-state blockade.
record.consequences: Traffic interrupted; broader economic damage not independently quantified.
record.relationship: Distinct dated protest from R4-AES-001 July 9, 2021 Oshoek blockade and June–July 2021 leads; not a continuation inferred from shared organisers.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
record.official_rationale: Organisers called for democratic reform, rights protections and an end to royal rule; the blockade aimed to exert economic pressure on the monarchy.
record.context: Action took place on King Mswati III’s birthday, within the continuing pro-democracy campaign.
record.uncertainty: Post lists differ between original reports. News24 describes six hours, but no common hour-by-hour chronology exists for all posts. Ministry statement confirms only Ngwenya operating normally later that day.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Same-day Ngwenya restoration is a partial endpoint for a multi-post episode; no all-post six-hour interval.
